title: Belgian police advise disabling the default admin user on smart devices after attacks on supermarket cooling systems
date_note: The page gives no earlier day than its publication day.
geo_basis: Regional Computer Crime Unit in Liège, as named by Security.NL
summary: Security.NL reports that Belgian police advise disabling the default "admin" user on smart devices and creating a separately named account. Commissaris Christophe Axen of the Regional Computer Crime Unit in Liège also advises changing default passwords, never reusing passwords, using two-factor authentication and researching devices before buying them. Security.NL says the advice follows attacks on online-accessible cooling systems at supermarkets in seven countries.
plain: Belgian police say people should switch off the default admin account on smart devices, use a differently named account, and secure their passwords, after attacks on supermarket cooling systems, Security.NL reports.
exec: Police advice on default admin accounts applies to internet-connected devices a business runs, following attacks on supermarket cooling systems, per Security.NL.
action: Belgian police (Commissaris Axen) advise disabling the admin user and creating a differently named account, changing default passwords, not reusing passwords and using two-factor authentication.

evidence.quote: Ik raad altijd aan om de 'admin-gebruiker' uit te schakelen en een ander account met een verschillende naam te maken.

validation.note: Security.NL only; the police statement is relayed, the police original was not read.

review.note: Compared title, date 25 Nov, advice list, seven-country supermarket cooling context and evidence quote against the Security.NL page; all match; single_source is right
